ground_truth.title: 2026 CRM Comparison Chart
ground_truth.author: GURUS - Drupal
ground_truth.main_content:
Finding the right Customer Relationship Management (CRM) software for your organization can be challenging, but don't worry, I'm here to help!

Whether you run a small business or are in the process of scaling, there are plenty of options available to meet your needs.

With the right CRM system, you'll be able to streamline your operations and grow your business with ease. As a service-based company, for example, you'll want to prioritize robust features such as customer service management, sales automation, marketing automation, and lead tracking.

Investing in CRMs that offer e-commerce integration, customer behavior tracking, and inventory management capabilities can greatly benefit retailers.

Thanks to advancements in technology, global software companies have modernized their offerings to include a multitude of components designed specifically for different industry verticals.

This guide will compare six top-ranking CRM software platforms: Salesforce, HubSpot, Monday.com, NetSuite CRM, Zoho CRM, and Zendesk. Below, we'll break down each industry and the features offered by each CRM software so you can confidently decide which system is the right fit for you.

Business Size NetSuite CRM HubSpot Monday.com Salesforce Zoho CRM Zendesk
Small (1-99 employees) Generally considered too complex and expensive for small businesses, but offers substantial benefits at this level Very attractive due to its user-friendly interface and free CRM offering, perfect for businesses with limited budgets Its flexibility and visual project management tools make it a good option for small businesses looking to streamline operations Might be overwhelming due to its complexity and cost, but Salesforce Essentials is tailored for small businesses Highly attractive due to its affordability and the breadth of features available even in lower-tier plans Good choice for small businesses focusing on improving customer service with an easy-to-use interface
Medium (100-999 employees) Perfect for medium-sized businesses looking for an all-in-one solution for CRM, ERP, and finance Offers sufficient scalability and advanced features in its paid plans to support growing demands Suitable for medium-sized businesses, especially for those prioritizing project management and team collaboration Highly suitable due to its scalability, extensive ecosystem, and customizable features Offers the scalability and customization medium-sized businesses need to grow and adapt Suitable for medium-sized businesses with a strong need for customer support and service tools
Large (+1000 employees) May not meet the needs of enterprise-level companies, and lacks robust features compared to others While it can serve large enterprises, it might lack the depth of customization and integration capabilities May not be the first choice as a dedicated CRM for large enterprises but can be an effective tool within a larger tech ecosystem Ideal for large enterprises requiring complex customization, integration, and global scale Can serve large enterprises, especially with its highest-tier plans, but may not be as widely adopted as others Can serve large enterprises, particularly in the customer support domain, though may need to be part of a broader CRM and tech ecosystem

Industry Focus (Basic/Best) NetSuite CRM HubSpot Monday.com Salesforce Zoho CRM Zendesk
Manufacturing Basic Best Best Best Basic Best
Wholesale Distribution Basic Best Basic Best Best Basic
Hospitality Basic Best Basic Best Best Basic
Healthcare Basic Best Basic Best Best Best
Retail Basic Best Basic Best Best Best
Professional Services Basic Best Best Best Basic Basic

Core Features (Basic/Best) NetSuite CRM HubSpot Monday.com Salesforce Zoho CRM Zendesk
Contact Management Basic Best Best Best Best Basic
Customer Support Basic Best Best Best Basic Best
Marketing Automation Basic Best Best Best Best Basic
Sales Force Automation Best Best Best Best Best Best
Customizability Best Basic Best Best Basic Basic
Reporting and Analytics Basic Basic Best Best Basic Basic
Integration Capabilities Best Basic Basic Best Best Basic
Mobile Access Basic Best Basic Best Best Best

Pricing NetSuite CRM HubSpot Monday.com Salesforce Zoho CRM Zendesk
Software/Users (Pricing per Month) NetSuite CRM is included with any Suite at no additional costs Free tools available with limited functionality, and plans starting at $20USD/month for Starter Free tools available with limited functionality, and plans starting at $13CAD/user per month for Basic Pricing starts at $25USD/user for Starter Suite, which offers limited functionality Pricing starts at $14USD/user for Standard, which offers limited functionality Zendesk offers Sales and Service pricing which starts at $19USD/user for Sell Team, which offers very limited functionality
Scaling up NetSuite CRM scales up with your NetSuite instance without any extra fees Two tiers after Starter: Professional ($800USD/month) and Enterprise ($3600USD/month) with extra fees for Sales Hub and Customer Hub functionality Three tiers after Basic: Standard ($17CAD/user) and Pro ($26CAD/user), and Enterprise with pricing available upon request Pricing grows quickly as a business scales up. Tiers include: Professional ($80USD/user), Enterprise ($165USD/user), and Unlimited ($330USD/user) Three tiers after Standard: Professional ($23USD/user) and Enterprise ($40USD/user), and Ultimate ($52USD/user) for those who require Zoho Analytics Three tiers after Sell Team: Sell Growth ($55USD/user), Sell Professional ($115USD/user), Sell Enterprise ($169USD/user). Service tiers are priced higher with pricing available upon request

What is a CRM?

Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems have emerged as indispensable tools for companies seeking to maintain strong relationships with their customers in the ever-evolving landscape of business technology.

At its core, a CRM is a sophisticated platform designed to streamline the management of all interactions and relationships between a company and its customers, prospects, and service users.

By centralizing data from multiple communication channels, CRMs enable companies to improve customer service, increase sales, and enhance marketing strategies by providing a 360-degree view of the customer journey.

Whether it's tracking customer interactions, managing sales pipelines, automating marketing campaigns, or generating actionable insights through data analytics, CRM systems are designed to increase efficiency and improve customer satisfaction.

As companies strive to navigate the complexities of today's markets, it is more important than ever to understand the critical role CRM software plays in achieving sustainable growth and customer loyalty.

Best-of-breed vs. Integrated Systems

In the dynamic landscape of digital business solutions, navigating the decision between specialized services and comprehensive platforms is a pivotal crossroads for growing businesses.

This choice often boils down to a debate between Best-of-Breed solutions and Integrated Systems (ERPs), a decision that hinges heavily on what you value most: specialized functionality or seamless collaboration.

Best-of-breed solutions emerge as the clear frontrunner for businesses that place a premium on having the highest functionality within a specific domain. These platforms excel in their specialization, offering depth and a range of features unmatched by more generalized systems.

Yet, it's crucial to weigh the hidden costs associated with this route. The complexity of managing multiple specialized systems can lead to higher operational costs, from maintaining diverse IT infrastructures to providing extensive training for employees across various platforms.

Conversely, for organizations where collaboration and streamlined operations take precedence, Integrated Systems or ERPs present a compelling argument. ERPs excel in fostering interdepartmental synergy, reducing the need for redundant communications, and simplifying cross-functional processes under a single technological umbrella.

This consolidation can significantly cut down on the overheads associated with managing separate systems. However, the trade-off often lies in the breadth of functionality, as the native capabilities of an ERP system may not always reach the specialized heights of Best-of-Breed solutions.

For instance, while a Best-of-Breed CRM might offer an expansive set of features dedicated to customer relationship management, an ERP's CRM component, although integrated, might not be as comprehensive.

Therefore, if your business seeks a well-rounded financial system with competent CRM features, leaning towards an ERP could serve you well, marrying financial oversight with customer engagement capabilities in a unified system.

Ultimately, the decision between Best-of-Breed versus Integrated Solutions pivots on aligning your business's priorities with the right digital ecosystem, ensuring that your choice not only supports current operational efficiencies but also scales with your future growth ambitions.

CRM Requirements by Industry

The best CRM for a given industry depends on specific needs like integration with industry-specific tools, compliance with regulatory requirements, and the ability to handle the particular sales and service processes of that industry.

Wholesale Distribution

Features like inventory management integration, customer order history, and supply chain management capabilities are key.

Hospitality

CRMs should focus on customer experience management, booking system integration, and personalized marketing automation.

Construction

CRMs that offer strong project management features, integration with construction management software, and robust mobile access are beneficial.

Healthcare

Compliance with healthcare regulations (e.g., HIPAA in the U.S.), patient relationship management, and integration with electronic health records (EHRs) are crucial.

Retail

E-commerce integration, customer loyalty program management, and sales forecasting are important features.

Professional Services

Project management, time tracking, invoice management, and high customizability to suit various service models are valuable.

Core CRM Features

Here are some of the core features CRMs provide their users:

Contact Management

Centralized database for customer information.

Organizes contact details and interaction history.

Facilitates personalized communication.

Customer Support

Unified platform for managing inquiries and service requests.

Tracks interaction history for efficient issue resolution.

Automates ticket routing and prioritization.

Marketing Automation

Automates repetitive marketing tasks (emails, social media, campaigns).

Segments customers for personalized marketing.

Measures campaign effectiveness with analytics.

Sales Force Automation

Predicts future sales volumes using historical data.

Helps in strategic planning and resource management.

Identifies trends and areas for sales process improvement.

Customizability

Adapts dashboards, reports, and modules to business needs.

Ensures CRM evolves with business growth and changes.

Reporting and Analytics

Transforms data into actionable insights.

Tracks performance across sales, marketing, and service.

Provides real-time visibility into key metrics.

Integration Capabilities

Seamless data flow between CRM and other software systems.

Eliminates data silos, improving process efficiency.

Enhances customer experience through consistent communication.

Mobile Access

Enables access to CRM data and tasks from anywhere.

Supports real-time updates and communication.

Ensures productivity away from the office.
